about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Dimas, California
about.longDescription: San Dimas sees its share of everyday traffic — commuters merging onto SR-57 and SR-210, drivers cutting across Arrow Highway to reach the foothills or the fairgrounds. In the most recent year on record, the city logged 139 injury collisions and 204 people hurt, along with 3 traffic deaths. Numbers like that represent real people dealing with medical bills, missed work, and a lot of uncertainty about what comes next. We handle personal injury claims at no upfront cost — you only pay a fee if you recover compensation. Our team can review what happened and explain your options under California law. California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require action in as little as six months, so it helps to move sooner rather than later. If a crash near SR-57, SR-210, or Arrow Highway has upended your routine, you don't have to sort through the legal side alone.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the chance to recover anything at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in San Dimas?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city road or public vehicle, the deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do injury collisions tend to cluster in San Dimas?
items.answer: Public-record collision counts show activity concentrated along SR-57, SR-210, and Arrow Highway, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't barred entirely.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency — we only collect a fee if you recover compensation. There's no cost to you just to get information about your options.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are a personal injury practice. Our team can evaluate your situation and help you understand your legal options.
